findings.reason: Untrusted source: ppl_header.entries_count is a raw __le32 field of the on-disk Partial Parity Log header (include/uapi/linux/raid/md_p.h:420-428), read from the member device by ppl_load_distributed() via sync_page_io() into a single 4096-byte page; a corrupted or malicious disk / tampered PPL area crosses the trust boundary into kernel state exactly like the seed's wire count. Violated invariant (validated-vs-used asymmetry): the only validation applied to the loaded header is the CRC checksum, signature, and generation comparisons in ppl_load_distributed() -- none of them constrains entries_count -- and no clamp against the known array capacity PPL_HDR_MAX_ENTRIES (=64, the entries[64] member that ends the 4KB page) exists anywhere on the read/recovery path; rg over the whole file shows the only entries_count guards are the >0 test at line 315 and the WRITE-path fullness test io->entries_count == PPL_HDR_MAX_ENTRIES at lines 280-281, i.e. the producing direction enforces the cap that the consuming direction omits -- the mirror asymmetry of the seed (CMD_SUBMIT clamp vs RET_SUBMIT none). Unsafe use: ppl_recover() line 976 iterates the unclamped on-disk count and line 977 takes &pplhdr->entries[i] past the 64-entry array for entries_count > 64, an OOB read of whatever follows the page; each OOB-fetched pp_size/checksum then drives the while (pp_size) sync_page_io loop (lines 991-1005) and, when the CRC happens to match, ppl_recover_entry() (line 784) uses the fetched pp_size/data_size as data_disks and strip_sectors loop bounds. The same unclamped count also drives the offset-advance loop at lines 1151-1153 (pplhdr_offset += le32_to_cpu(pplhdr->entries[i].pp_size) >> 9), steering subsequent header reads to attacker-chosen disk offsets. Impact: OOB read past a 4KB page plus attacker-controlled iteration/offsets during array assembly and recovery (ppl_load -> ppl_load_distributed -> ppl_recover, called at raid5-ppl.c:1420), i.e. crash/DoS and unvalidated on-disk data feeding parity recovery writes; counterevidence checked: no entries_count<=PPL_HDR_MAX_ENTRIES or <=(PAGE_SIZE-...) validation anywhere in drivers/md (rg entries_count over drivers/, fs/, block/ shows no other raid consumer), CRC is attacker-forgeable by anyone who can write the PPL area, and the write path's own cap (line 281) proves the kernel-known maximum exists and is simply not enforced on the read path.

candidates.reason: ppl_recover() consumes on-disk pplhdr->entries_count with no clamp against PPL_HDR_MAX_ENTRIES (64); reported as the finding (see findings[0]).

Second unclamped consumer of the same on-disk count in ppl_load_distributed(): 'for (i = 0; i < le32_to_cpu(pplhdr->entries_count); i++) pplhdr_offset += le32_to_cpu(pplhdr->entries[i].pp_size) >> 9;' -- same missing cap, advances the header-search offset using OOB-fetched pp_size values; part of the reported finding.

Write/producing path enforces the cap: io->entries_count == PPL_HDR_MAX_ENTRIES at lines 280-281 blocks adding entries and ppl_submit_iounit (line 445-456) loops only over the kernel-maintained io->entries_count; this is the enforcing sibling direction proving the asymmetric validation.

ppl_recover_entry() consumes e->pp_size/e->data_size (disk __le32) as data_disks = data_size / pp_size and strip_sectors loop bounds with no local cross-check against chunk_sectors/block_size upper bounds; for i>=64 these values are themselves OOB-fetched past the page. Counted as part of the reported chain.

Seed subsystem present in s07 but PATCHED: usbip_pack_ret_submit unpack clamps 'if (rpdu->number_of_packets < 0 || rpdu->number_of_packets > urb->number_of_packets) rpdu->number_of_packets = 0;' (482-485) and usbip_recv_iso validates 'np <= 0 || np > USBIP_MAX_ISO_PACKETS' and zeroes urb->number_of_packets before bailing (685-693), so the seed's error-unwind poisoned-count is fixed here; additionally excluded from findings by the seed-never-reportable rule.

ws_inc()/ws_dec() loop over 'count' supplied by the dm persistent-data btree walker (kernel-computed array element count, dm-block-manager sized), not a raw disk/wire count stored into a shared object; per-iteration values (ws_d.root) go through dm_tm_inc/dm_bitset_del block validation. No untrusted count left in shared state for a later error path.

limitations: Bounded sweep: the search ranked deserialization/count-store files by wire-endian (le/be*_to_cpu, get_unaligned, ntoh*) count/num_/nr_ hits and deep-read drivers/md/raid5-ppl.c, drivers/md/dm-era-target.c, and the seed usbip family; high-hit files only located and NOT deep-read include fs/ocfs2/refcounttree.c, fs/ocfs2/xattr.c, fs/f2fs/super.c, fs/ntfs3/fslog.c (range_count at 4565), drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath12k|ath10k wmi/htt, drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu_discovery.c, drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_ddp.c, idpf_virtchnl.c, bnxt.c, drivers/accel/qaic/qaic_control.c, and dm-zoned-metadata.c.

The reported finding's attacker is a corrupted/tampered disk or PPL area (on-disk metadata trust boundary), weaker than the seed's remote network peer; the CRC/signature checks do not constrain entries_count but forging them requires write access to the PPL area, and exploitation impact beyond the OOB page read and attacker-steered recovery offsets (what memory follows the page, whether recovered data is exposed) was not proven.

No compilation, static analysis, or runtime reproducer was run (assigned tree is read-only and building md/raid5 PPL recovery requires a crafted block device); all conclusions come from direct numbered source reads (awk-verified line windows) of snapshots/s07 only.

urb->actual_length / number_of_packets completion consumers in drivers/usb (btusb, xhci-ring, ehci-sched, mon_bin, media UVC, sound/usb) were enumerated by file list but their error/teardown paths were not individually walked before the finalize directive.
